image:image.image:title: Why Solo Founder Burnout Destroys Promising Startups Before Product Market Fit
image:image.image:caption: Solo founder burnout happens quietly when one builder absorbs every technical failure, customer objection, and financial pressure alone.

image:image.image:title: Why Building Alone Starves Your Startup Of Distribution And Revenue
image:image.image:caption: Thousands of polished solo products die with fewer than ten paying customers because nobody ran distribution while code was written.

image:image.image:title: The Echo Chamber Trap Why Solo Builders Ship Products Nobody Wants
image:image.image:caption: Confirmation bias thrives in isolation when nobody with equal ownership pushes back on flawed product assumptions.

image:image.image:title: Why Venture Investors Quietly Reject Solo Founders As A Single Point Of Failure
image:image.image:caption: Institutional seed investors evaluate founder team resilience first because early products pivot while founding partnerships endure.

image:image.image:title: Why A Two Founder Team Ships Twice As Fast And Wins Every Competitive Market
image:image.image:caption: Startup velocity compounds weekly when two aligned cofounders eliminate context switching and run product and market loops in parallel.
